While dragging, use the arrow keys to move the item.
Press space again to drop the item in its new position, or press escape to cancel.

deleteKeyword.takenOff_other: Taken off {{count}} records, and out of the keyword filter.

errorBoundary.title: Something broke
errorBoundary.body: A view failed to render. Try again re-mounts it without reloading the page.

boot.takingLong: Your local database is taking longer than usual to open. Another jojo tab may be holding it — closing the others usually frees it.

firstRun.title: How would you like to start?
firstRun.description: jojo keeps everything on this machine, so this is yours to decide. Neither answer is final — you can load the demo data or clear every record later, from Settings.

demo.title: Explore with demo data
demo.detail: A worked job search to look around in — twelve applications, a timeline, a stocked vault. Nothing in it is yours, and clearing it later takes one press.

empty.title: Start empty
empty.detail: No demo records at all. Every page opens on its empty state, and the first thing in jojo is something you added.

recovery.title: jojo cannot read its database
recovery.body: Your records are still on this machine. jojo has not changed or replaced anything, and it will not load the demo data over them — a store that reseeded itself to look healthy would turn this into permanent data loss.
recovery.downloadHint: Writes the rows that could be read to a file
recovery.downloadNothing: The database could not be read at all, so there is nothing to write out
recovery.freshHint: Deletes the database and starts jojo as if it were new
recovery.readable_one: {{count}} row was readable — download it before anything else, since starting fresh deletes it.
recovery.readable_other: {{count}} rows were readable — download them before anything else, since starting fresh deletes them.
recovery.unreadable: Nothing could be read out of the store, so there is nothing to download. Try again first: a database another tab is holding open fails this way and recovers on its own.
recovery.confirmTitle: Delete the database and start fresh?
recovery.confirmBody: This deletes jojo's local database and everything still in it, then starts again from nothing — including the question a first run asks about whether to begin with the demo data or empty. It does not repair anything and there is no undo. If you have not downloaded the readable rows yet, cancel and do that first.

labelFilter.label: Filter by keyword
labelFilter.none: No keywords yet — add one to filter by it.

keywordChip.taken: Another keyword already has that name.

welcome.title: A little about you
welcome.description: Drafts sign off with your name, and the scout scores against what you are looking for. All of it stays on this machine, and all of it is optional — you can fill it in later under Profile.
welcome.rest: The rest — links, target roles, the terms the scout matches on — lives under <anchor>Profile</anchor>.

onboarding.tourDescription: A walk through the real pages — a spotlight on each part, what it is for, and you try each thing as you go. It never types, saves or changes anything for you, and it keeps your place if you stop.
onboarding.always: It is always there under How to use, so saying no now costs nothing.

setup.optional: Every one of these is optional and you can set it up later under Settings.

model.title: Connect a model
model.body: This is what makes jojo agentic rather than a filing cabinet: it can then answer questions about your search, write follow-ups and drafts, and run the Job Scout pipelines that keep your records complete and watch for postings. Point it at a model on your own machine and nothing leaves the device.

reader.title: Let it read your documents
reader.body: Without this the assistant can see a document’s name and nothing else. Run MarkItDown on this machine — two commands, below — and it can read what is inside your CVs, cover letters and saved postings when it drafts and answers.

crash.title: Crash reports and usage
crash.description: Two separate things, both on — turn off either one here or later in Settings. Neither can carry your records: not an application, a document, a note, a profile or a conversation.
crash.inError: The error message and where in jojo it happened.
crash.inStack: The stack trace, which names the code that failed.
crash.neverRecords: Your applications, documents, notes, profile or conversations.
crash.neverSecrets: Your API keys, the addresses you use, your home directory, or any email address — these are stripped out before a report is written, not before it is sent.
crash.where: In this browser and in the jojo extension, crash reports stay on this device: nothing is uploaded, and a backup file does not carry them. You read them yourself under Settings. On the jojo phone app the same report is also sent to Google's Firebase Crashlytics, which adds your device model, its operating system version, and a random id it uses to count how many people hit the same crash — no name, no account, nothing tied to you. Usage counts, the second switch below, go to Google Analytics from every version including this one.
crash.keepHint: The error and where it happened. Stays on this device in the browser.
crash.shareHint: Counts only — which screens are opened, how often. Never what is in them.
crash.usageNote: The second one is the only thing jojo sends about what you DO, and it can only ever say things from a fixed list — “the vault was opened”, “an application was added”, “there are 6–20 of them”. It cannot name an employer, a role, a file or anything you typed, because those words are not in the list. It goes to Google Analytics so we can see which parts of jojo are worth more work.
crash.later: You can change either of these at any time under Settings, and turning one off also discards what it kept.

extension.title: Keep the postings you apply to
extension.body: Job adverts come down, often before you hear back. The browser extension saves a posting as it reads today, into your own vault — and it is also how the Job Scout reads the boards you follow.
